stem: A client receiving ifosfamide is prescribed mesna. What is the purpose of mesna in this regimen?

options.A: Reduce the incidence of ifosfamide-induced hemorrhagic cystitis
options.B: Treat chemotherapy-induced neutropenia by stimulating neutrophil production
options.D: Treat established chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting

rationale: Current mesna labeling identifies mesna as a cytoprotective prophylactic agent used to reduce the incidence of ifosfamide-induced hemorrhagic cystitis. It does not act as a granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, a cardioprotective agent for anthracyclines, or an antiemetic. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Recognize mesna as a uroprotective/cytoprotective medication used prophylactically with ifosfamide to reduce hemorrhagic cystitis risk.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_locator: Highlights and Full Prescribing Information §1 Indications and Usage: mesna injection is a cytoprotective agent indicated as a prophylactic agent in reducing the incidence of ifosfamide-induced hemorrhagic cystitis; limitation states it is not indicated to reduce hematuria from other pathological conditions
source_claim_supported: Mesna is indicated prophylactically to reduce the incidence of ifosfamide-induced hemorrhagic cystitis.
